gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in Apple's own spec words, a base M3 MacBook Air or Pro runs a second external display only with the lid closed. A two-screen extender hangs on the open lid, so on a base M3, as on base M1 and M2 and the MacBook Neo, it gets one native screen and needs a display driver for the second. Apple says the M4 MacBook Air drives two external displays alongside its own open screen.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages: Macworld 'Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026', itechguides '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' and RTINGS 'Best Portable Monitors'. Macworld names plain M1 and M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo as one-monitor machines and says the Trio 3 Pro then needs software, but it says nothing about M3. Its own Trio 3 Pro review (Simon Jary, Apr 2 2026, not in ChatGPT's results) says Macs above 'a standard M1/M2/M3' need no download, which leaves the base M3 open. Apple's spec pages settle it: a second display only with the lid closed. itechguides mentions DisplayLink 'protected-content limitations' only in general and ties no chip limit to any product. The RTINGS page text had no compatibility content. None of the pages says that on macOS protected video can go blank on every screen while a DisplayLink display is connected. That point comes from Plugable's knowledge base about DisplayLink products in general.
decides: This changes the pick by laptop. On a base M1, M2 or M3 MacBook or a MacBook Neo, only one added screen runs natively, so a one-screen unit is the clean pick: Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS (14.1-inch) or Duex Float 2 Pro (16-inch stacked). Our records list both on a single native USB-C video path with no driver. On those Macs the Trio 3 Pro, any dual FOPO and the FOPO S788 run the extra screens through a driver. When that driver is DisplayLink, Plugable says protected video may stay blank on all screens while it is connected. On an M4 MacBook Air, or a Mac with a Pro or Max chip, two native screens work, so the Trio 3 Pro with one cable per screen and no driver is a reasonable best-overall pick. The page should ask which Mac or chip the shopper has before it names a two-screen pick.

findings.label: Video path on plain M1/M2 Macs and MacBook Neo (named reviewer)
findings.value: Free Mobile Pixels software needed to run both screens; one-cable use needs the software
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld (Simon Jary, Apr 2 2026)
findings.note: Jary: 'plain (non-Pro/Max) M1 and M2 Macs plus the new MacBook Neo are limited to connecting just a single monitor. To work with the Trio 3 Pro users of those Macs will need to download and install free software (rather like DisplayLink)'. Two USB-C cables come in the box, one per screen. Running both screens from one cable needs the software, plus a power adapter for full brightness (up to 65 W passthrough). The review implies a base M3 needs no software, but Apple's M3 spec pages above allow a second display only with the lid closed.
